# dsh-peak-cost
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that adds one ambient line under the composer:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
It answers three questions about the session you are in:

1. **Is DeepSeek billing in peak hours right now?**
2. **How much has this session cost so far, in U

S dollars?**
3. **What is left in your DeepSeek account?**
Hovering the line opens a panel with the cost attribution: the billing window and the time until it
flips, the account balance and both wallets, and a per-category table showing what each kind of cont
ent cost when it first entered the context versus what it costs on every later call that re-sends it
nt cost when it first entered the context versus what it costs on every later call that re-sends it.
The screenshot above is unedited: the line sits beside the shipped turn/step counter and token meter
, and reads `● Off-peak · ≈ $0.338 · bal $7.27` for a session at 9 turns and 264 steps with a 99.6%
Off-peak · ≈ $0.338 · bal $7.27` for a session at 9 turns and 264 steps with a 99.6% cache hit rate.
## Behavior
| Slot | `conversation.composer.dock` (below the composer card, beside the shipped activity and cont

ext-usage entries) |
| Scope | Per session |
| Updates | Spend follows every settled model call; the

status label re-evaluates against the clock every 30 s; the balance refreshes every 60 s |
| Locale
s | English and Chinese, following the app's language setting |
### Balance
Next to the session estimate the line also shows your DeepSeek account balance:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
It is read from the Host's account Remote (`ctx.remote.account.getBalance`) every 60 seconds and whe
never the window regains focus — the same call the Settings → Account page makes — and **both wallet
kinds are summed**: the recharge wallet plus any bonus/grant wallet, which is why it can differ fro
m a single number on a top-up page. The panel always lists both.
The account face is a Typert Remote namespace rather than a plain service, so the plugin captures it
through a scoped `ctx.inject(['remote.account'], …)` and still falls back to `ctx.remote.account` o
n the root context. That keeps it independent of load order: the cost line renders immediately, and
the balance appears as soon as the transport is reachable.
The balance is optional in every direction: a signed-out account, an API-key-only setup, a failed re
ad, or a build without the account transport all simply drop it, leaving the cost line intact. Nothi
ng is cached to disk.
## Where the money went
Hovering the line opens a themed panel (fixed-positioned above the composer, closes on leave or Esca
pe) with the attribution:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Each row answers two different questions:
- **First time** — what that content cost when it entered the context, billed as cache-miss input, o

nce.
- **Re-sent** — what it has cost on every later call that carried it, billed as cache-hit input

ce.
- **Re-sent** — what it has cost on every later call that carried it, billed as cache-hit input.
So "what did the web search data cost in this session?" is one row: the first fetch at the miss rate
plus every re-send at the hit rate. A search result that arrives once and stays in the conversation
is billed as input exactly once and as cache for the rest of the session — which is why 18k tokens
of web data cost about a cent rather than 18 × the input rate.
### How the split is made
Every call reports real billed usage. The fold keeps a running estimate of the context by category a
nd splits each call's prompt:
- **cache-miss tokens** go to the content added since the previous call, proportional to its size —

a new search result, a new tool output, a new reply;
- **cache-hit tokens** go to everything already
in context, proportional to its size.
Per-call totals are the provider's own numbers, so category costs add up to the real bill and only t
he split between categories is an estimate (four characters per token). Output is listed separately
because it is not context. Replaced or compacted content is subtracted as it leaves the context, so
the "In context" column tracks the live surface rather than a running sum.
## Install
The package is a Harness **bundle**: it declares `dsh.bundle.patch` and a `dsh.client` half, so inst
alling it in a profile mounts both the Host projection and the Web entry.
Install the package spec `github:ogidimitrov/dsh-peak-cost` as a bundle — from the Plugins page of t
he app, or from an agent session through the plugin manager's `install_bundle` action with that spec
an agent session through the plugin manager's `install_bundle` action with that spec as the target.
[该节后续省略]
### Why this number and your balance can disagree
The figure is a **list-price equivalent**, computed from the session log; it never reads your wallet
. Three things make a wallet diverge from it:
- **Granted or bonus credit is consumed first.** DeepSeek deducts from granted/bonus balances before

a topped-up balance, so a topped-up number can stay flat while usage accrues.
- **The balance is no

t streamed.** It is read on demand from the platform; a panel left open shows what it read.
- **Not
every call is in the log.** Session-title generation and some compaction work never commit an `assis
tant/message`, so they cost money this estimate cannot see.
Use the platform's usage page for the authoritative charge; this line is for watching a session's sh
usage page for the authoritative charge; this line is for watching a session's shape while it runs.
## Known limitations
- **An estimate.** It prices reported tokens at list rates. It is not a bill: nothing here reads you

r balance or the provider's invoice.
- **Only settled model calls count.** Calls that never commit a
n `assistant/message` — session-title generation, some compaction work — are not in the log and are

not counted. Failed attempts that report usage without a settled message are likewise skipped.
- **O
ne session.** Subagent sessions have their own logs and their own dock lines; this number is the ses

sion you are looking at.
- **Unknown routes.** A model id that matches no card is counted in the mes

sage total but priced at zero; the tooltip reports how many.
- **Search/Fetch.** Standalone Search a
nd Fetch API charges are not modelled.
